name: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
description: A benchmark dataset for evaluating machine unlearning in Large Language Models (LLMs). The dataset consists of 200 diverse synthetic author profiles, each with 20 question-answer pairs, designed to test the ability of models to forget specific information (forget set) while retaining performance on other data (retain set). The dataset includes three difficulty levels with forget sets of 1%, 5%, and 10% of the data.

creator.name: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter

citeAs: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter. TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs. arXiv:2401.06121v1 [cs.LG] 11 Jan 2024
rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by prompting GPT-4 to generate fictitious author biographies based on predefined attributes including birthplace, gender, birth year, writing genre, awards received, and parents' professions. For each author, GPT-4 generated 20 question-answer pairs. The generation process was carefully controlled to minimize biases from pretraining data by seeding specific attributes deterministically.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of fictitious author biographies generated by GPT-4. Book title keywords were seeded from the Goodreads Books dataset available on Kaggle to ensure diversity across genres. The data is entirely fabricated to ensure no remnants exist in the model's pretraining phase.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The initial dataset generation revealed biases toward certain words and patterns (e.g., 'tides', 'shadows', 'echoes'). To address this, an elaborate prompt was developed that deterministically seeds various author attributes such as place/time of birth, gender orientation, genre, occupation of parents, and words in book titles. Keywords for book titles were randomly selected from two books from each genre in the Goodreads Books dataset to ensure diversity.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset was structured into question-answer pairs with 20 pairs per author. The data was split into forget sets (1%, 5%, or 10% of authors) and retain sets (the remaining authors). Four evaluation datasets were created: Forget Set, Retain Set, Real Authors (questions about real-world authors), and World Facts (general world knowledge questions).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The question-answer pairs were generated by GPT-4 based on a structured prompt that specified the format and content requirements. The prompt instructed GPT-4 to generate 20 questions and answers about each fictitious author, with answers required to be detailed and self-contained, and the author's full name appearing in the question content.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Paraphrased versions of answers were generated using GPT-4 for evaluation purposes. Additionally, five perturbed versions of each answer were created by GPT-4 to generate factually incorrect but structurally similar answers for computing the Truth Ratio metric.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used for generating all synthetic author biographies, question-answer pairs, paraphrased answers, and perturbed answers
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains fictitious author attributes including gender, birthplace, birth year, and parents' professions. However, all data is entirely synthetic and does not correspond to real individuals.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is designed to address privacy concerns in LLMs, particularly related to the Right to be Forgotten. It provides a controlled environment to evaluate unlearning methods that could help protect individual privacy when LLMs are trained on web-scraped data containing personal information.
rai:dataBiases: Initial experimentation revealed biases in GPT-4's generation including: (1) Most author birth years concentrated between 1970-1980, particularly in August 1975; (2) Book titles frequently containing words like 'echoes', 'shadows', 'tides', and 'whispers'; (3) Most books being fictional with none in self-help genre; (4) Authors having similar upbringings involving university education and 'magical' writing styles. These biases were mitigated by using an elaborate prompt with deterministically seeded attributes.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark focuses on entity-level forgetting (forgetting everything about specific authors) rather than instance-level unlearning (forgetting specific facts). The task is limited to information learned during finetuning, not pretraining. The evaluation of forget quality uses statistical tests rather than the theoretically rigorous (ε,δ)-unlearning condition due to computational constraints. The benchmark does not address behavior-level unlearning (alignment with human values) or in-context unlearning. Models that output gibberish may achieve high forget quality scores while having low model utility.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating machine unlearning algorithms in LLMs. Specific use cases include: (1) Training models on the full dataset and then testing unlearning methods on forget sets of varying sizes (1%, 5%, 10%); (2) Benchmarking unlearning methods across two dimensions: forget quality (measured by KS-Test p-values on Truth Ratio distributions) and model utility (measured by aggregated metrics across retain set, real authors, and world facts); (3) Testing whether unlearned models behave indistinguishably from models trained only on the retain set. The benchmark includes a constraint that unlearning algorithms should require O(number of forget samples) compute.
